function.mechanism: Dissociates into calcium and chloride ions that modify ionic strength and pH behavior, support firming/textural effects, and influence thermal reaction pathways in some processed foods.

adi.basis: EFSA FAF 2019 identified a human reference value of 40 mg chloride/kg bw/day for risk assessment; this is a reference value rather than an explicitly labeled ADI in the opinion abstract.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA concluded exposure to chloride from E507/E508/E509/E511 does not raise a safety concern at reported use levels; high-percentile exposure in some child groups was slightly above the 40 mg/kg bw/day reference value.

fda.notes: Listed under 21 CFR Part 184 GRAS framework; use limited by current good manufacturing practice with category-specific maximum as-served levels.

adi.basis: JECFA entry reports ADI as NOT LIMITED (non-numeric).

concerns.summary: EFSA reported some animal data suggesting chloride may contribute to increased blood pressure, and therefore used human data to derive a chloride reference value for safety assessment.

A 2022 zebrafish food-safety toxicology study found developmental/cardiac/neural toxicity above 0.4% CaCl2 and complete embryo mortality at 0.8%-1.6% in acute exposure, indicating concentration-dependent toxicity in experimental models.
Recent heating-model studies reported CaCl2 can reduce acrylamide but may increase HMF/furan-related process contaminants in some matrices, indicating a process-chemistry tradeoff.

no_concern_confirmed: EFSA 2019 concluded chloride exposure from E507/E508/E509/E511 does not raise a safety concern at reported uses.
EFSA summary states no concern for genotoxicity and carcinogenicity in the assessed chloride group.
FDA affirms calcium chloride as GRAS in 21 CFR Part 184 with CGMP conditions.
JECFA lists calcium chloride ADI as NOT LIMITED.
No IARC monograph classification entry for calcium chloride was identified.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA reported mean exposure estimates at/below the 40 mg chloride/kg bw/day reference value, while 95th-percentile exposure was slightly above this value in some younger age groups.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulatory convergence indicates low risk at authorized use levels (EFSA no-safety-concern conclusion, FDA GRAS, JECFA not-limited ADI). Remaining uncertainty comes from high-percentile child exposure relative to EFSA's chloride reference value and concentration-dependent effects in experimental studies.
key_factors: EFSA 2019 conclusion of no safety concern at reported use/use levels
EFSA reference value of 40 mg chloride/kg bw/day with slight 95th-percentile exceedance in some child groups
FDA GRAS status with explicit 21 CFR 184.1193 use conditions and maximum levels
No IARC Group 1/2A/2B listing for calcium chloride
